---
title: "Survival weights with individual visit times: a bug in every version up to 1.3.2"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(ipw)
library(survival)
stored <- readRDS("survival-weights-bug.rds")
cases <- stored$cases
data("haartdat", package = "ipw")
cases$haartdat_first$data <- haartdat
cases$haartdat_cens$data <- haartdat
versions <- names(stored$by_version)
old_res <- function(v, nm) stored$by_version[[v]]$results[[nm]]
fmt <- function(x, d = 2) trimws(formatC(x, format = "g", digits = d))
```

## Summary

`ipwtm()` with `family = "survival"` and `type = "first"` (or `"cens"` for
censoring weights) computed **wrong weights when subjects have their own
visit times**, that is, when the rows of different subjects do not start and
end at the same time points. The probability of each row used the increase
in the baseline hazard since the previous time point *in the whole data
set*, instead of since the start of the row.

* The bug is in **every version on CRAN, from ipw 1.0 (2011) to ipw 1.3.2**.
  All `r length(versions)` versions were installed and run on the same data
  for this page; they give identical weights.
* Data in which all subjects share the same time points, such as `haartdat`
  or data prepared as in Example 2 of `?ipwtm`, were **not affected**.
* With individual visit times the weights were far off: in the example below
  some weights differ from the correct ones by a factor of more than 30.
* The development version fixes it: each row uses the baseline hazard over
  its own interval `(tstart, timevar]`.

## 1. What the weights should be

For `type = "first"`, each row of a subject covers an interval
`(tstart, timevar]` until the first exposure (for example the start of a
treatment). With a Cox model for the time to exposure, the probability of
*no* exposure during the row is

$$
P(\text{no exposure in } (t_\text{start}, t]) =
\exp\{-[H_0(t) - H_0(t_\text{start})]\, e^{\beta^\top x}\},
$$

where $H_0$ is the cumulative baseline hazard. The probability of exposure
at the end of the row is one minus this. The weight of a row is the product
of the inverse probabilities of the rows of that subject so far (and the
numerator model's probabilities, for stabilised weights). Censoring weights
(`type = "cens"`) use the probability of remaining uncensored the same way.

## 2. What older versions computed

Older versions computed the hazard of a row as

$$
H_0(t) - H_0(t_\text{prev}),
$$

where $t_\text{prev}$ is the time point just before $t$ **among all times
in the data**, of any subject. When every subject has rows at the same time
points, $t_\text{prev}$ is the start of the row, and the two are the same.
When subjects have their own visit times, $t_\text{prev}$ is usually later
than $t_\text{start}$, so part of the hazard during the row is left out: the
probability of no exposure is too high and the probability of exposure too
low. Weights of exposed rows come out too large, and weights of unexposed
rows too small.

## 3. A worked example with three patients

```{r tiny-data}
d <- cases$tiny$data
d
```

Patients 1 and 3 are at risk from day 10 and day 5 to day 20. Patient 2 is
exposed at day 15 and patient 1 at day 20, so the baseline hazard increases
at day 15 and at day 20. The times in the data are 5, 10, 15 and 20.

The Cox model and its cumulative baseline hazard. Here $H_0$ is computed by
hand from the risk sets (Efron's method, as `coxph()` uses), without
`basehaz()` or `survfit()`:

```{r tiny-fit}
fit <- coxph(Surv(tstart, time, a) ~ l, data = d, ties = "efron")
r <- exp(coef(fit) * d$l)                    # relative hazard of each row

# Efron cumulative baseline hazard from the risk sets
H_efron <- function(start, stop, event, r) {
  et <- sort(unique(stop[event == 1]))
  inc <- vapply(et, function(t) {
    S0 <- sum(r[start < t & stop >= t])      # risk set at time t
    D <- which(stop == t & event == 1)       # events at time t
    k <- length(D)
    sum(1 / (S0 - (seq_len(k) - 1) / k * sum(r[D])))
  }, numeric(1))
  cum <- cumsum(inc)
  function(t) vapply(t, function(s) {
    j <- which(et <= s)
    if (length(j)) cum[max(j)] else 0
  }, numeric(1))
}
H0 <- H_efron(d$tstart, d$time, d$a, r)
H0(c(5, 10, 15, 20))
```

For each row, the correct hazard uses `tstart`; the old one used the
previous time in the data:

```{r tiny-table}
times <- sort(unique(d$time))
t_prev <- c(NA, times)[match(d$time, times)]
hz_correct <- (H0(d$time) - H0(d$tstart)) * r
hz_old <- (H0(d$time) - ifelse(is.na(t_prev), 0, H0(t_prev))) * r
p_correct <- ifelse(d$a == 1, 1 - exp(-hz_correct), exp(-hz_correct))
p_old <- ifelse(d$a == 1, 1 - exp(-hz_old), exp(-hz_old))
w_correct <- ave(1 / p_correct, d$id, FUN = cumprod)
w_old <- ave(1 / p_old, d$id, FUN = cumprod)

tab <- data.frame(id = d$id, interval = paste0("(", d$tstart, ", ", d$time, "]"),
                  old_interval = paste0("(", ifelse(is.na(t_prev), "-", t_prev), ", ", d$time, "]"),
                  hazard_correct = hz_correct, hazard_old = hz_old,
                  weight_correct = w_correct, weight_old = w_old)
knitr::kable(tab, digits = 3)
```

The rows `(10, 20]` of patient 1 and `(5, 20]` of patient 3 were at risk at
day 15, when patient 2 was exposed, but the old calculation started counting
at day 15 and missed that part of the hazard. Patient 1, exposed at day 20,
gets a weight of `r round(w_old[2], 3)` instead of `r round(w_correct[2], 3)`.

The same numbers from the package. Every old version gives the old weights,
and the development version gives the correct ones:

```{r tiny-package}
w_dev <- ipwtm(exposure = a, family = "survival", denominator = ~ l, id = id,
               tstart = tstart, timevar = time, type = "first", data = d)$ipw.weights
data.frame(id = d$id, interval = tab$interval,
           ipw_1.2.1.1 = old_res("1.2.1.1", "tiny")$weights,
           ipw_1.3.2 = old_res("1.3.2", "tiny")$weights,
           this_version = w_dev, by_hand = w_correct)
```

```{r tiny-checks}
# old versions = the old calculation above; this version = the correct one
max(abs(old_res("1.0", "tiny")$weights - w_old))
max(abs(w_dev - w_correct))
```

## 4. Is my data affected?

Only rows that enter the exposure (or censoring) model matter, and only if
their `tstart` is not the time point just before their `timevar` among all
times in the data. This function counts such rows:

```{r check-fun}
rows_affected <- function(data, id, tstart, timevar, exposure) {
  d <- data[order(data[[id]], data[[timevar]]), ]
  in_model <- ave(d[[exposure]], d[[id]], FUN = function(z) cumsum(cumsum(z)) <= 1) == 1
  times <- sort(unique(d[[timevar]]))
  t_prev <- c(-Inf, times)[match(d[[timevar]], times)]
  first_time <- d[[timevar]] == times[1]
  sum(in_model & !first_time & d[[tstart]] != t_prev)
}
rows_affected(haartdat, "patient", "tstart", "fuptime", "haartind")
rows_affected(cases$own_first$data, "id", "tstart", "time", "a")
nrow(cases$own_first$data)
```

`haartdat` has no affected rows: all patients have rows every 100 days. In
the data with individual visit times nearly every row is affected. If the
count is 0 for your data, the old versions gave the correct weights.

## 5. All versions from 1.0 to 1.3.2

The same cases were run in every version of ipw on CRAN (in separate R
sessions, with the script `data-raw/make-survival-bug-article-data.R`) and
compared with the correct weights computed by hand as above:

* **haartdat**: treatment weights (`type = "first"`) and censoring weights
  (`type = "cens"`) from the `?ipwtm` example; common time grid.
* **own times**: 300 subjects, each with their own visit times, unstabilised
  (`numerator = NULL`) and stabilised (`numerator = ~ x`), and censoring
  weights.
* **own times on a common grid**: the same data, with every row split at
  all times in the data (as in Example 2 of `?ipwtm`).

```{r correct-weights, include = FALSE}
correct_weights <- function(d, exposure, id, tstart, time, num, den, type) {
  o <- order(d[[id]], d[[time]])
  ds <- d[o, ]
  ev <- ds[[exposure]]
  sel <- ave(ev, ds[[id]], FUN = function(z) cumsum(cumsum(z)) <= 1) == 1
  prob <- function(covs) {
    if (is.null(covs)) return(rep(1, nrow(ds)))
    act <- ds[sel, ]
    f <- as.formula(paste0("Surv(", tstart, ", ", time, ", ", exposure, ") ~ ",
                           paste(covs, collapse = " + ")))
    m <- coxph(f, data = act, ties = "efron")
    X <- model.matrix(as.formula(paste("~", paste(covs, collapse = " + "))), ds)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
    rr <- drop(exp(X %*% coef(m)))
    H <- H_efron(act[[tstart]], act[[time]], ev[sel], rr[sel])
    dH <- (H(ds[[time]]) - H(ds[[tstart]])) * rr
    p <- if (type == "cens") exp(-dH) else ifelse(ev == 1, 1 - exp(-dH), exp(-dH))
    p[!sel] <- 1
    p
  }
  w <- ave(prob(num) / prob(den), ds[[id]], FUN = cumprod)
  w[order(o)]
}
refs <- list(
  haartdat_first = correct_weights(haartdat, "haartind", "patient", "tstart", "fuptime",
                                   c("sex", "age"), c("sex", "age", "cd4.sqrt"), "first"),
  haartdat_cens = correct_weights(haartdat, "dropout", "patient", "tstart", "fuptime",
                                  c("sex", "age"), c("sex", "age", "cd4.sqrt"), "cens"),
  own_first = correct_weights(cases$own_first$data, "a", "id", "tstart", "time",
                              NULL, c("x", "l"), "first"),
  own_first_stab = correct_weights(cases$own_first_stab$data, "a", "id", "tstart", "time",
                                   "x", c("x", "l"), "first"),
  own_cens = correct_weights(cases$own_cens$data, "dropout", "id", "tstart", "time",
                             "x", c("x", "l"), "cens"),
  common_grid_first = correct_weights(cases$common_grid_first$data, "a", "id", "tstart", "time",
                                      NULL, c("x", "l"), "first"))
now <- lapply(cases[names(refs)], function(cs) eval(cs$call, list(data = cs$data))$ipw.weights)
```

```{r versions-table, echo = FALSE}
status <- function(x, ref) {
  if (is.null(x)) return("not run")
  if (!is.na(x$error)) return(if (grepl("No type specified", x$error)) "no type = \"cens\"" else "error")
  d <- max(abs(x$weights / ref - 1))
  if (d < 1e-8) "correct" else paste0("wrong (", fmt(d), ")")
}
labels <- c(haartdat_first = "haartdat, first", haartdat_cens = "haartdat, cens",
            own_first = "own times, first", own_first_stab = "own times, first, stabilised",
            own_cens = "own times, cens", common_grid_first = "own times on a common grid")
rows <- lapply(versions, function(v) {
  bv <- stored$by_version[[v]]
  st <- if (!isTRUE(bv$installed) || is.null(bv$results)) rep("could not be run", length(labels)) else
    vapply(names(labels), function(nm) status(bv$results[[nm]], refs[[nm]]), "")
  c(v, st)
})
rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c(paste0("this version (", utils::packageVersion("ipw"), ")"),
  vapply(names(labels), function(nm) {
    d <- max(abs(now[[nm]] / refs[[nm]] - 1)); if (d < 1e-8) "correct" else paste0("wrong (", fmt(d), ")")
  }, ""))
tab <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, rows), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(tab) <- c("Version", labels)
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

The numbers in brackets are the largest relative difference between a
version's weights and the correct weights (2 means one weight is three times
too large or too small). Versions 1.0 to 1.0-11 had no `type = "cens"`.

```{r identical, include = FALSE}
ok <- vapply(versions, function(v) {
  r <- old_res(v, "own_first")
  !is.null(r) && is.na(r$error) && isTRUE(all.equal(r$weights, old_res("1.0", "own_first")$weights, tolerance = 1e-10))
}, logical(1))
```

All `r sum(ok)` versions give the same weights as ipw 1.0 for the
individual visit times, to 1e-10. The calculation was the same from the
first release; the rewrite in 1.3 kept it, and its comparison with 1.2.1.1
used `haartdat`, where the two agree.

How far off are the weights? For the unstabilised weights:

```{r size}
old_w <- old_res("1.3.2", "own_first")$weights
summary(old_w / refs$own_first)
c(largest_weight_old = max(old_w), largest_weight_correct = max(refs$own_first))
```

## 6. If you used an older version

1. Check your data with `rows_affected()` above. If it returns 0, your
   weights were correct.
2. Otherwise, recompute the weights with the fixed version. With an older
   version you can get correct weights by first splitting every row at all
   times that occur in the data, so that all subjects share one time grid;
   the last column of the table in section 5 shows that this gives the correct
   weights in every version. For example:

```{r split, eval = FALSE}
split_common_grid <- function(d) {
  grid <- sort(unique(c(d$tstart, d$time)))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(r) {
    cuts <- grid[grid > d$tstart[r] & grid < d$time[r]]
    s <- c(d$tstart[r], cuts); e <- c(cuts, d$time[r]); k <- length(s)
    data.frame(id = d$id[r], tstart = s, time = e, x = d$x[r], l = d$l[r],
               a = c(rep(0, k - 1), d$a[r]))   # exposure on the last piece only
  }))
}
```

The weight at the end of an original row is the weight on its last piece.

## 7. The code: before and after

```{r show-code, include = FALSE}
show_lines <- function(x, lines) {
  x <- gsub("\t", "  ", x)
  cat(sprintf("%4d  %s", lines, x[lines]), sep = "\n")
}
```

The code below is taken from the source packages on CRAN (stored with this
article by `data-raw/make-survival-bug-article-data.R`); line numbers are
those of `R/ipwtm.R` in each version. Only the denominator model is shown;
the numerator model had the same code.

### ipw 1.0 (2011)

```{r code-1.0, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
show_lines(stored$old_code[["1.0"]], 147:162)
```

Line 148 makes a list of **all distinct times in the data**
(`tempdat$timevar`, the end times of all rows of all subjects). Lines
152-153 take the increase of the cumulative baseline hazard between
neighbouring times in that list, and line 155 attaches it to each row by its
end time. Lines 158-160 use that increase as the hazard of the row. The
start time of the row (`tstart`) is not used at all.

### ipw 1.2.1.1 (the last version before the rewrite)

```{r code-1.2.1.1, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
show_lines(stored$old_code[["1.2.1.1"]], 186:202)
```

The same calculation (lines 187, 191-192, 194, 197); only the censoring
weights (`type = "cens"`, line 200) were added.

### ipw 1.3.2 (CRAN, after the rewrite)

```{r code-1.3.2, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
show_lines(stored$old_code[["1.3.2"]], 491:513)
```

The rewrite kept the calculation: `u_times` is the list of all distinct end
times (line 492), `step_haz` the increase between neighbouring times (line
501), merged onto the rows by their end time and used as the hazard of the
row (line 513).

### The fix (this version)

```{r code-now, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
src <- if (file.exists("../../R/ipwtm.R")) readLines("../../R/ipwtm.R") else character()
from <- grep("Hazard over each row's own interval", src)
to <- grep("inst_haz <- ", src)
if (length(from) == 1 && length(to) == 1) show_lines(src, from:to) else
  cat("(source of this version not found)\n")
```

The cumulative baseline hazard is now evaluated at both ends of each row's
own interval, `timevar` and `tstart`, and the difference is the hazard of
the row. This is the calculation that `type = "all"` (new in this version)
already used. For data on a common time grid the weights are unchanged; the
package tests check this against the stored results of ipw 1.2.1.1 for
`haartdat` and other data.

### Tests

The package tests compare the weights with a baseline hazard computed by
hand from the risk sets, as in section 3, for `type = "first"` and
`type = "cens"`, on data with individual visit times, with tied times and
with follow-up starting below 0, with the rows in random order. This is the
test (from `tests/testthat/test-audit2-ipwtm.R`; the helper functions
`r2_H0()`, `r2_surv_ref()` and `r2_irregular()` are defined at the top of
that file):

```{r test-code, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
tf <- "../../tests/testthat/test-audit2-ipwtm.R"
tsrc <- if (file.exists(tf)) readLines(tf) else character()
from <- grep("^r2_H0 <- function", tsrc)
start <- grep("survival first/cens equal an independent by-hand Efron interval hazard", tsrc)
end <- if (length(start)) start - 1 + which(tsrc[start:length(tsrc)] == "})")[1] else NA
if (length(from) == 1 && length(start) == 1 && !is.na(end)) {
  cat(tsrc[from:(from + 9)], "...", tsrc[start:end], sep = "\n")
} else cat("(test file not found)\n")
```

The same comparison fails for every version up to 1.3.2, as section 5 shows.
Another test checks that `type = "first"` and `type = "all"` agree when every
subject is exposed at most once (`tests/testthat/test-audit-ipwtm.R`). The
tests run on Linux, macOS and Windows with every change to the package.
